title: CI Orchestration Audit & Gate Map
purpose: Map the existing integral test-platform authorities to the four roadmap CI gates before changing orchestration behavior.

pr_fast_regression.intent: Fast pull-request feedback using delta-selected authorities, static acceptance validators, and shared full-stack runners.
pr_fast_regression.trigger_contract: pull_request path filters with workflow_dispatch fallback

residuals.description: There is no single aggregate PR Fast Regression decision that summarizes all selected fast authorities for one candidate SHA.
Sixteen individual heavy-workflow fallbacks still coexist with the five shared-stack clusters; intentional fallback versus duplicate automatic execution is not centrally governed.

full_regression.intent: Run the complete regression set for a candidate rather than only delta-selected authorities.
full_regression.trigger_contract: currently pull_request path-filtered and workflow_dispatch, not an unconditional candidate gate
full_regression.candidate_contract: exact PR head checkout where implemented

residuals.description: No single orchestration entry point forces all P0 authorities plus full frontend regression against the same candidate SHA.
The workflow named Full frontend regression is path-filtered and covers frontend regression, but is not by itself the roadmap Full Regression gate for the complete product.

deep_nightly.intent: Scheduled heavy combinations, failure/recovery variants, legacy regressions, and broader diagnostic coverage.
deep_nightly.trigger_contract: manual/PR authorities exist; no canonical scheduled Deep/Nightly orchestration is registered

residuals.description: No canonical schedule trigger bundles the expensive failure/recovery and legacy authorities into a Deep/Nightly run.
Deep-run evidence has no single aggregate result or retained manifest identifying the exact candidate and all executed authorities.

release_acceptance.intent: One release-candidate decision combining build/package, PostgreSQL/migration/startup authority, acceptance matrices, and downstream PO acceptance state.
release_acceptance.trigger_contract: separate PR/manual workflows; no central release-acceptance orchestrator
release_acceptance.candidate_contract: exact candidate identity is present in key release and database workflows but not aggregated into one decision

residuals.description: No single Release Acceptance orchestration binds package/build, PostgreSQL migration/startup, zero-residual and acceptance results to one candidate SHA.
PO acceptance state is not yet part of an automated release decision; this is intentionally completed in roadmap Phase 8/9, not invented inside F7-01.
Backup -> restore -> startup -> data-integrity proof is not yet registered as a release gate dependency and remains a downstream release-readiness residual.

cross_cutting.delta_planner_policy: fail open on uncertainty; synchronize compares only newly pushed delta; non-synchronize/manual paths run requested authorities
cross_cutting.candidate_identity_assessment: strong in the audited shared runners and named full/release workflows; no cross-workflow aggregate candidate contract yet
cross_cutting.evidence_assessment: per-workflow evidence exists, but naming, retention and aggregate decision semantics are heterogeneous
